week.title: Asia FX Outlook 2027: Rotation underway but tech currencies should lead
week.desc: ASIA/PACIFIC: The recent sell-off in oil prices has provided some much-needed relief to South Asian currencies. Looking into 2027, and assuming the dollar does start to soften, we prefer to back the tech-linked currencies of North Asia. These currencies are backed by large current account surpluses – surpluses which could be coming home

week.title: Latam FX Outlook 2027: Banxico abandons the peso
week.desc: LATIN AMERICA: It has been a mixed year for Latam FX, where only the higher yields of the Brazilian real and Mexican peso have allowed those currencies to deliver a net total positive return against the dollar. In 2027, we think the real can outperform the forwards, but are worried about Banxico’s neglect of the peso. Chile’s peso might prove a little more resilient, too

week.title: EMEA FX Outlook 2027: Restrictive policy remains the key FX anchor
week.desc: CENTRAL AND EASTERN EUROPE: EMEA FX should remain supported by restrictive policy and attractive carry, but performance will increasingly diverge. We favour HUF, ZAR and TRY, while CZK remains supported and PLN faces headwinds. Global yields, energy prices, fiscal risks and geopolitics remain key drivers

week.title: FX volatility in 2027: In need of shock therapy
week.desc: EUROPE: Why is FX volatility so low? Even a 6% fall in the Nasdaq barely budges USD/JPY these days. Have FX markets found a general equilibrium, or is there some kind of separation between geopolitics and macro? We think the answer lies more in the structure of FX trading and do not rule out jump risk if the shock is big enough

week.title: G10 FX Outlook 2027: It’s hard to look beyond the Fed

week.title: FX outlook 2027: Seven key risks

week.title: Credit Selloff Lures Bargain Hunters to ‘Stock Picker’s Market’
week.desc: MFS Investment Management’s Pilar Gomez-Bravo and J.P. Morgan Asset Management’s Iain Stealey see opportunities in beaten-up credit after the recent selloff, particularly in lower-rated and subordinated debt. Both stressed the need for selectivity, with Gomez-Bravo calling it a “stock picker’s market” and Stealey favoring subordinated debt from strong investment-grade companies over traditional high yield, as heavy supply and higher rates make a return to relentless spread tightening unlikely. (Source: Bloomberg)

week.title: FX Daily: Higher US real rates dominate

There is no reason to fight this trend near term

(Source: Bloomberg)
